what: Unlock PDF removes the password from a PDF that you can open, and takes away limits on printing, copying and editing. You get a normal PDF that opens straight away on any device.

It is useful for bank statements, payslips, tickets and reports that arrive locked with a password you know, but that you need to print, merge, sign or upload somewhere that does not accept protected files.

The decryption is done in your browser by qpdf, a well-known open source PDF program, compiled to run on your device. The file and the password are never uploaded. The tool cannot find or break a password you do not know.
uses: Remove the password from monthly statements so you can save and print them without typing it every time.
Merge or edit a locked file
Many PDF tools refuse protected files. Unlock first, then merge, split or sign.
Some PDFs open freely but block printing or copying text. Unlock removes these limits.
Websites for applications and taxes often reject password-protected PDFs.
tutorial: Click the box that says "Click or drop a locked PDF here", or drag the file onto it.
See what kind of lock it has
The tool checks the file. It either says "This PDF needs a password to open" or lists what is not allowed, such as printing or copying.
If a password is needed, type it in "Password of this PDF". Use "Show" to see what you typed.
Press the button or the Enter key. A wrong password gives a red message so you can try again.
When the message says "Unlocked", click "Download unlocked PDF". The new file ends in -unlocked.pdf.
features: Works with every standard PDF password: AES 256-bit, AES 128-bit, RC4 128-bit and RC4 40-bit.
Printing, copying, editing and form limits are removed together with the password.
Either the password that opens the file or the owner password works.
Shows whether the file needs a password or only has restrictions, and which actions are blocked.
The file and password stay on your device; nothing is sent to a server.
Pages, text, pictures, links and bookmarks are kept exactly as they were.

example.title: Worked example: a locked bank statement
example.text: Amira downloads statement-march.pdf. Her bank locks it with her date of birth. She drops it in, the tool says "This PDF needs a password to open", she types 14081992 and presses Enter. The message reads "Unlocked. The new file opens without a password", and she downloads statement-march-unlocked.pdf to merge it with the other months.

tips: Passwords are case-sensitive: check Caps Lock if the password is refused.
Banks often use your date of birth, account number or ID number as the password. Check the email that came with the file.
Keep the unlocked copy somewhere safe, since anyone can now open it.
To lock it again with your own password, use Protect PDF.
problems: The message says the password is not right
Check capital letters, spaces and the keyboard language, and try the password from the email or letter again.
The message says there is nothing to unlock
The file has no password and no restrictions, so it can be used as it is.
The file could not be read
The PDF may be damaged or not a real PDF. Download it again and retry.
I do not know the password
This tool cannot recover it. Ask the sender for the password or for an unlocked copy.
